required_outcomes: Recognises that the provider and the tenant still hold different dates: the provider has Monday 1 September 10am to 12pm and nothing on 8 September; the tenant believes 8 September.

Asks the tenant, promptly given 1 September is the coming Monday, whether she can be in on Monday 1 September 10am to 12pm or, failing that, Thursday 4 September 1pm to 4pm, and tells her plainly that 8 September is not booked and that nobody was due on 30 August.
Does not record or confirm a visit date until the tenant has agreed to one, and tells the provider the tenant is being asked so the 1 September slot is not wasted.
acceptable_alternatives: Phoning the tenant rather than emailing, as long as her answer is recorded before any date is confirmed.
Asking the provider in the same step whether any slot nearer 8 September exists, provided the tenant is still offered the two dates the provider gave.
positive_behaviours: Apologises for the conflicting notifications and explains the 30/08 date was an error in the agency's own record.
Sets a short follow-up (before Monday 1 September) so the provider can be told in time if the tenant cannot make it.
red_flags: Telling the tenant to take the date the provider gave her as correct without stating which date that is.
Escalating to a human when asking the tenant settles it.
prohibited_actions: Telling the tenant the visit is on 8 September, or the provider that the tenant has agreed 1 September, before she has.
critical_failures: Sending a confirmed-appointment notice for 1 September (or 8 September) before both the tenant and the provider have agreed that date.
